review.title: Drain review: `door-tape-grammar-1` HOTFIX, the county door accepts the recorder's reels again (Opus 5.5 implementer at max effort; F-LSR1-0, P0)

bookkeeping.rowText: The county door accepts `playbookUses` (each `{kind:'playbook_use', atTick in [0, durationTicks] non-decreasing, playbook}` validated by the client's `validatePlaybook` with the tape's contract, seed and difficulty) and `motorActions` (each `{t in [0, durationTicks) non-decreasing, kind motor_grade|motor_haul, point in [-256, 256]}` via the client's `validateMotorActions`), both optional, at most `maxEntries` each; absent and empty accepted, null and any unknown key still refused; nine mutations each red. RED first: the real recorder's reel got 400 `bad_payload` twice on the base and is stored, ranked and read back through `?reel=` at the tip. 372 to 412 door checks per backend; accounts, mp 528, stats green; `RunTape.ts` byte-identical, hash unchanged {PIN}. DEPLOYED (the deploy restarts `goldrush-ledger`, whose door is this module): a human who secures a run banks a county standing again after twenty days. **F-DTG1-1 (P0 continuation `door-tape-grammar-2`): the door still refuses `prospector_dispatch`, `context_action recover` and multiplayer `agent_orders`, so a reel with a dispatch is still refused until it lands.** F-DTG1-5: the function bundle grew 387 to 508 KB (a validators-only module later).
bookkeeping.statusPhrase: the county door accepts the recorder's reels again after twenty days of refusing every human standing, and its three remaining refused verbs have their continuation running
